title: Theft
summary: Taking someone's movable property without their consent, intending to permanently keep it.
what_to_do: File a police complaint / FIR at the nearest police station. Theft is a cognizable offence, meaning police can register an FIR and investigate without needing a magistrate's order first.
punishment: Up to 3 years imprisonment, or fine, or both

title: Voluntarily causing hurt
summary: Intentionally causing bodily pain, disease, or infirmity to another person.
what_to_do: File a police complaint. If injuries are serious, get a medical examination done immediately as medical evidence strengthens the case.
punishment: Up to 1 year imprisonment, or fine up to Rs. 10,000, or both (simple hurt); higher for grievous hurt

title: Criminal intimidation
summary: Threatening someone with injury to their person, reputation, or property, to cause alarm or force them to act against their will.
what_to_do: File a police complaint with any evidence of the threat (messages, witnesses, recordings).
punishment: Up to 2 years imprisonment, or fine, or both

title: Rape
summary: Rape is sexual intercourse with a woman against her will, without her consent, or with consent obtained by fear of death/hurt, fraud, or when she is unable to understand the nature of the act.
what_to_do: Report to the police immediately or call 112. Preserve evidence (clothing, body samples) — do not bathe before a medical examination. The victim's medical exam in a government hospital is free.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment of not less than 10 years, extendable to life imprisonment, with fine

title: Assault on a woman to outrage her modesty
summary: Assaulting or using criminal force on a woman intending to or knowing it will outrage her modesty (e.g., touching, groping, staring, or physical advances).
what_to_do: File a police complaint / FIR. This is a cognizable, bailable offence. Preserve any messages, CCTV footage, or witnesses.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both

title: Dowry death
summary: Death of a woman caused by burns or bodily injury within 7 years of marriage, when it is shown that she was subjected to cruelty or harassment for dowry before her death.
what_to_do: Report to the police immediately. Police must register an FIR and the death is investigated as a dowry death if the 7-year and cruelty conditions hold.
punishment: Imprisonment of not less than 7 years, extendable to life imprisonment, with fine

title: Cruelty by husband or relatives of husband
summary: A husband or his relative subjecting a woman to cruelty — conduct that drives her to suicide, or causes grave injury/danger to life, limb or health (mental or physical), or dowry-related harassment.
what_to_do: File a complaint / FIR, usually at the police station in the jurisdiction where the cruelty occurred. Keep evidence like messages, photographs, and medical records.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, with fine

title: Punishment for murder
summary: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
what_to_do: Call the police / 112 immediately. Do not disturb the crime scene. Cooperate fully with the investigation.
punishment: Death or life imprisonment, with fine

title: Attempt to murder
summary: Doing an act towards committing murder, with the intention to kill, capable of causing death (e.g., shooting, stabbing or poisoning).
what_to_do: File an FIR immediately. Preserve physical evidence and get medical examination of the injured person.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years, with fine

title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
summary: Intentionally causing hurt that is serious — such as emasculation, permanent loss of sight/hearing/limb/joint, disfigurement, fracture, or an injury endangering life or lasting more than 20 days.
what_to_do: File a police complaint and get the injury medically verified. Keep hospital records and doctor's certificate as proof of grievous hurt.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, with fine

title: Wrongful restraint
summary: Voluntarily obstructing a person from proceeding in any direction in which they have a right to proceed (e.g., blocking someone's path).
what_to_do: File a police complaint. This is a non-cognizable offence, so you may need a court order (complaint before a magistrate) if police do not act.
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine, or both

title: Wrongful confinement
summary: Wrongfully restraining a person so as to prevent them from moving beyond certain limits — i.e., being locked inside or held somewhere against their will.
what_to_do: This is a serious matter — call the police / 112. If released, file an FIR describing where and for how long you were confined.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both

title: Kidnapping
summary: Taking or enticing a minor (under 16 for boys / under 18 for girls, or any person of unsound mind) away from their lawful guardian without consent.
what_to_do: Report to the police immediately — do not wait. Provide a photo, last known location, and description to help the search.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, with fine

title: Snatching
summary: Snatching means dishonestly taking movable property out of someone's possession or from their person without consent — a new specific offence in BNS 2023 (e.g., chain snatching, phone snatching).
what_to_do: File an FIR immediately. Note the description of the person/vehicle. Police can register a case; snatching is a cognizable offence.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, with fine

title: Extortion
summary: Intentionally putting a person in fear of injury and thereby dishonestly inducing them to deliver property, valuable security, or money (e.g., threats to pay 'protection' money).
what_to_do: Report to the police with any evidence — messages, call recordings, or witnesses. Threats of extortion are often also covered by criminal intimidation.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both

title: Robbery
summary: Theft or extortion committed with violence or the fear of instant violence, or while taking property out of a person's immediate presence (e.g., mugging at knife-point).
what_to_do: Call the police / 112. File an FIR at the police station where the offence happened. If injured, get medical treatment first.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, with fine (higher in aggravated cases)

title: Dacoity
summary: Robbery committed by five or more persons acting together.
what_to_do: Call the police / 112 immediately. File an FIR; do not disturb any evidence at the scene.
punishment: Life imprisonment or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, with fine

title: Criminal breach of trust
summary: When someone entrusted with property dishonestly misappropriates or converts it to their own use (e.g., an employee taking company money, misuse of entrusted funds).
what_to_do: File a police complaint with proof of the entrustment (agreement, records). If the person is an employee, also consider disciplinary action.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both

title: Cheating
summary: Deceiving a person fraudulently or dishonestly to induce them to deliver property, or to do/omit something they would not otherwise do (e.g., fake job offers, online fraud, cheque fraud).
what_to_do: File an FIR with all evidence — chat transcripts, payment receipts, fake documents. For online fraud, also report to the cyber cell (cybercrime.gov.in).
punishment: Up to 3 years imprisonment, or fine, or both; up to 7 years where it involves delivery of property (e.g., fraud like the old IPC 420)

title: Defamation
summary: Making or publishing any imputation concerning a person intended to harm their reputation (in words, signs, or visible representations). Truth for the public good can be a defence.
what_to_do: Defamation is not cognizable — you can either file a criminal complaint before a magistrate or a civil defamation suit for damages. Keep records of the defamatory content.
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both

title: Defective goods / deficient service complaint
summary: Right to file a complaint against a seller or service provider for defective goods, deficient service, unfair trade practice, or overcharging.
what_to_do: File a complaint with the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (for claims up to Rs. 1 crore). Keep purchase receipts, warranty cards, and communication records as evidence. No lawyer required to file.
punishment: Refund, replacement, compensation, or removal of defect as ordered by the Commission

title: Which forum to approach (jurisdiction by claim value)
summary: District Commission: claims up to Rs. 1 crore. State Commission: Rs. 1 crore to Rs. 10 crore. National Commission: above Rs. 10 crore.
what_to_do: Identify your claim amount, then file at the correct forum based on the thresholds above.

title: Deficiency in service
summary: 'Deficiency' means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming, or inadequacy in the quality, nature, or manner of service performance — required by law or promised under a contract (e.g., builder not completing on time).
what_to_do: When a service does not meet the promised standard or legal requirement, gather evidence of the shortfall and file a consumer complaint for the deficiency.
punishment: Compensation / remedy ordered by the Consumer Commission

title: Unfair trade practice
summary: Unfair trade practice covers false claims about goods/services, deceptive advertising, misleading 'free' offers, and certain manipulative contract terms in e-commerce and direct selling.
what_to_do: Collect the misleading advertisement/claim as evidence, then file a consumer complaint or approach the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) at cccp.gov.in.
punishment: Cease the unfair practice; compensation; CCPA can impose penalties

title: Procedure on admission of complaint (District Commission)
summary: After a complaint is admitted, the District Commission sends a copy to the opposite party, who must file a response within 30 days (extendable by 15). It then proceeds to settle the dispute on evidence.
what_to_do: If the opposite party does not respond, the matter proceeds ex parte (decided in your favour on your evidence). Attend all hearings and submit all evidence on time.

title: Findings / reliefs the District Commission can grant
summary: If the complaint succeeds, the District Commission can order removal of the defect, replacement of goods, refund of price with interest, compensation for loss/injury, discontinuation of unfair trade practice, etc.
what_to_do: The Commission decides the reliefs after hearing both sides — you do not have to request each specific relief; it can order what fits the case.
punishment: Reliefs under the Act (replacement, refund, compensation, stop practice)

title: Appeal against District Commission order
summary: A party aggrieved by a District Commission order can appeal to the State Commission within 45 days. An appeal requiring payment must deposit 50% of the amount in the prescribed manner.
what_to_do: If you lose your case at the District Commission, file an appeal to the State Commission within 45 days of the order, depositing 50% of the amount if payment is involved.

title: Duration and termination of tenancy (notice period)
summary: In the absence of a written agreement specifying duration, a lease is presumed month-to-month (for residential) or year-to-year (for agricultural/manufacturing). Requires 15 days' notice (month-to-month) or 6 months' notice (year-to-year) to terminate.
what_to_do: Check if you have a written rental agreement first, as it overrides this default rule. If none, this section's notice periods apply.

title: Rights and liabilities of landlord and tenant
summary: Lays out default obligations: landlord must disclose material defects in the property; tenant must not damage the property and must pay rent; tenant may make repairs necessary to prevent damage and deduct reasonable cost from rent.
what_to_do: If landlord refuses necessary repairs, document the issue in writing, get repair estimates, and you may deduct reasonable repair costs from rent (keep all receipts as proof).

title: What is a lease (definition)
summary: A lease is a transfer of the right to enjoy a property for a certain period (or in perpetuity), in exchange for rent or premium. The transferor is the lessor (landlord) and transferee is the lessee (tenant).
what_to_do: A tenancy gives you a legal right to occupy the property for the agreed term. Note whether your arrangement is a lease (written/unregistered) so you know your rights.

title: How a lease comes to an end (determination of lease)
summary: A lease ends by: expiry of the agreed term; determination of the lessor's interest; forfeiture for breach or denial of title; surrender by the lessee; or destruction of the property.
what_to_do: Know which ground applies to your situation — e.g., if the term has expired, the tenancy continues on the old terms unless validly terminated by notice.

title: Relief against forfeiture for non-payment of rent
summary: If a lease is forfeited for non-payment of rent, the tenant can avoid forfeiture by paying the arrears and the costs of the suit before the judgment is delivered.
what_to_do: If you are being evicted for non-payment of rent, pay the arrears plus costs as soon as possible to keep the lease alive — do not wait for the judgment.
